title: Libya Conflict Tracker Update — Mon Aug 31, 2026
summary: Libya's rival factions formally signed the UN-backed '4+4' election deal at UNSMIL headquarters in Tripoli on August 30, committing to elections within 24 months under a single executive authority. HoR, HSC, Haftar-camp, and GNU delegates all signed, and Dbeibah, Khalifa Haftar, Saddam Haftar, and Osama Hamad publicly welcomed the outcome. The legitimacy dispute is not fully resolved, however — the HoR and HSC now have a month to formally ratify the text, and an HoR member said eastern lawmakers were not consulted on the negotiating team's composition. No new military incidents or oil-infrastructure strikes were confirmed this period.

title: Libya Conflict Tracker Update — Sun Aug 30, 2026

title: Libya Conflict Tracker Update — Sat Aug 29, 2026
summary: Ten Western governments — Italy, France, Germany, Greece, Malta, the Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, the UK, and the US — issued a joint declaration on August 26 endorsing the Tunis '4+4' electoral deal as 'an important step,' even as Libya's own Presidential Council and High State Council continue to dispute its legitimacy. The next day, Qatar's Minister of State al-Khulaifi met Khalifa Haftar in Benghazi, the first senior Qatari visit to eastern Libya since the 2014 political split, and separately invited Saddam Haftar to Doha. No new military incidents, oil-infrastructure strikes, or migration disasters were confirmed this week.

title: Libya Conflict Tracker Update — Tue Aug 25, 2026
summary: Five days after the '4+4' committee initialled a draft election-law and elections-commission deal in Tunis, cracks opened over its legitimacy. Protesters blocked roads and burned tyres in several areas of Tripoli on August 25, reviving the civil disobedience campaign against prolonged electricity outages that began in late July.
